title: Sieve admin API has no auth — unsafe if exposed through reverse proxy
description: Scenario: operator puts nginx or traefik in front of the server and proxies /admin/ for convenience or SSL termination. Behavior: any user with HTTP access to the proxy can list/read/write/delete Sieve scripts for any configured user. The doc comment says 'Do not bind to a non-loopback address in production' but that warning is only in the struct doc, not surfaced at startup or in logs. Maintenance consequence: this will generate a CVE report. Even if you personally know not to do this, users will proxy it. Consider: log a warning at startup when the admin API is bound, add an explicit config acknowledgment key, or add optional shared-secret auth.
